entries.reason: cross-repo — root cause OUT OF SCOPE for stable-yield-accumulator
entries.subject: NudgeStreamer.collectNudge is PERMISSIONLESS and recomputes rewardPerSecond over the FULL duration on every deposit — a 1-wei donor can reset the streaming window at will (Linear-Depletion / rate-drift class)
entries.whyNotFiledAgainstSYA: C4: issues in parent/forked contracts where the root cause is OOS. Verified that SYA adds NO new capability — collectNudge is already fully permissionless, so an attacker resets the window directly for 1 wei plus gas; reaching it via SYA.claim is strictly MORE expensive (burns an NFT, pays actualPayment).
entries.machineEvidenceObtainedThisRun: Tier-3 Property 2 verified the resulting fixed point directly: standing float = donationRate x duration, cadence-independent (14,999.98e6 observed vs 15,000e6 expected at both 1-day and 6-hour cadences), fuzz-confirmed within 1% over T in [D/100, D/4].
entries.econRuling: Pure griefing, STRICTLY NEGATIVE-EV: the griefer's own potential batchMint take shrinks by exactly what they delay, no competitor is excluded, value is never destroyed or redirected. Damage is delay, not destruction.
entries.inScopeConsequenceFiled: DEDUP-004 — the donor's own honest claim cadence produces the same reset, so the float is a normal-operation property requiring no attacker.

New material: in the SYA integration the depositor is PERMISSIONLESS and the honest donor deposits at HIGH FREQUENCY, so rate-drift is present in practice even if the port is textually faithful to PhlimboV2 (where the depositor is privileged). Do NOT silently override run-24.

entries.reason: low reportability confidence — dust magnitude and byte-identical to pre-story-026 behaviour, but a real and distinct policy bypass; human adjudicates, not the scanner
entries.subject: nudgeSplit is silently unhonored below the rounding threshold: nudgeAmount floors to 0 and 100% of the payment routes to phlimbo, skipping the streamer branch entirely
entries.content: `nudgeAmount = (actualPayment * nudgeSplit) / 100` floors. When actualPayment < 100/nudgeSplit the nudge share rounds to zero, the `nudgeAmount > 0` guard skips the streamer branch, and phlimboAmount takes 100%. The configured donation policy is silently not applied. Rounding favours phlimbo over the nudge sink, NEVER the claimer.
entries.whyLowConfidence: With nudgeSplit=10 and a 6-dp reward token the threshold is actualPayment < 10, i.e. 1e-5 USDC, and every claim burns an NFT and requires non-zero skimmed yield — the NFT cost dwarfs any starve-the-nudge-pot gain by orders of magnitude. Not attacker-repeatable for profit.
entries.strongestArgumentForTriagingOut: code-scanner and econ-scanner (POS-003) independently confirmed the behaviour is BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL to pre-story-026 — the old safeTransfer sat under the same `> 0` guard — so story-026 introduces nothing new here.

distinctFrom.0da2e7cf4f (L-01, open): L-01 concerns actualPayment ITSELF flooring to 0. This concerns the SPLIT flooring to 0 while actualPayment is NON-ZERO — different divisor, different victim (the nudge sink, not the protocol), and it SURVIVES even if L-01 is fixed by re-guarding actualPayment > 0.
distinctFrom.ecc2d126dd (M-01, acknowledged): No decimal-config fail-open involved; this triggers with a fully and correctly configured token.
distinctFrom.RECON-001: RECON-001 is the actualPayment==0 path (BOTH legs skipped); this is the actualPayment>0 / nudgeAmount==0 path (only the nudge leg skipped).

entries.reason: declined an available collapse — folding this into ledger L-05 would silently overwrite that entry's central scoping qualifier with a contradicting fact
entries.subject: claim's inner loop over the CALLER-SUPPLIED exemptStrategies array is O(n*m) with m caller-controlled and duplicates not rejected
entries.content: The strategy loop (yieldStrategies, owner-bounded) contains an inner loop over the caller-supplied `exemptStrategies` calldata array, giving O(n*m) work with m FULLY CALLER-CONTROLLED. Duplicates are NOT rejected — the same registered strategy may appear m times and still pass validation, so m is unbounded independent of n.
entries.impact: Self-inflicted gas burn only: a caller cannot use this to grief anyone else, since each claim is independent and the cost lands on the caller. Secondary: claim's gas is not statically bounded, which matters for any bundler/relayer that pre-estimates.
entries.humanDecisionRequired: Ledger L-05 (d60ab75159, open) is explicitly scoped as 'owner/OOS-bounded, NOT a permissionless DoS'. This item identifies a CALLER-controlled, unbounded, duplicate-tolerant multiplier on the same loop. It is NOT an escalation (impact is self-inflicted), but the human should decide whether L-05's scoping sentence needs amending — the dedup stage should not make that edit silently.
entries.recommendation: Bound exemptStrategies.length by yieldStrategies.length, or reject duplicates.

entries.reason: victim is a downstream on-chain integrator; NOT covered by any existing ledger entry
entries.subject: canClaim loops i = 1..INFTMinterV2(nftMinter).nextIndex()-1, issuing one external balanceOf staticcall per dispatcher index
entries.content: nextIndex is monotonically increasing and controlled by the NFTMinter owner, never by SYA. View-only and primarily bot-facing (eth_call has generous gas), BUT any ON-CHAIN caller using canClaim as a gate inherits an unbounded, monotonically growing cost that can eventually exceed the block gas limit. Unchanged by story-026 except that nextIndex now resolves through INFTMinterV2.
entries.explicitlyNotCoveredBy: Ledger L-05 (d60ab75159) covers the yieldStrategies x authorized-clients product, NOT the nextIndex dispatcher loop — different array, different owner, different growth driver. Do not assume the SLITHER-002 -> L-05 reconciliation closes this.
entries.recommendation: Offer a paginated variant, or have bots use the O(1) balanceOf(caller, index) directly.

entries.reason: cannot be closed on the merits at this tier — the victim (ClaimArbitrage) is OUT OF this run's scope
entries.subject: Value-reporting views are readable mid-claim while the strategy set is transiently half-skimmed
entries.content: During claim's loop (:538-566) strategies at index < k have been skimmed and report zero surplus while those at index > k have not. The three views read that state unguarded, so an integrator reading them inside a callback window sees a value that is neither the pre-claim nor the post-claim figure.
entries.codeScannerRuling: Read-only-reentrancy check returned 'cleared with a caveat': no callback window is currently reachable — skimSurplus pays in hook-free stablecoins (USDC/USDT/DAI/USDS), strategies are owner-registered rather than permissionless, and the two external calls story-026 added or kept (collectNudge :599, collectReward :602) both run AFTER the loop closes, so the inconsistent window is already shut by then.
entries.whyStillParked: The REENTRANCY-READONLY pattern prescribes recording the finding even when the contract is itself safe, because the victim is a downstream integrator — and the project docs describe exactly such an integrator: ClaimArbitrage, which calls SYA.claim inside a Uniswap V4 unlockCallback. ClaimArbitrage is not in this run's scope, so neither the code-scanner nor this dedup stage can adjudicate reachability.
entries.humanDecisionRequired: Scope decision: bring ClaimArbitrage into scope for a reachability check, or accept the current 'safe by absence of hooks' argument on the record.
entries.relatedLedger: L-06 (90bcf3764e, open) covers getTotalYield's snapshot divergence and the paused-token view inconsistency — a DIFFERENT view defect on the same functions. Check for overlap if this is ever promoted.
